title: Nscale $35B IPO Delayed by AI Data Center Construction

body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- Nscale seeks a $35 billion IPO this month despite construction delays, safety violations, and cost overruns at AI data center sites across Europe and the US.
- The Glomfjord facility in Norway runs six months behind schedule with cooling system leaks, a transformer fire, and labor compliance issues discovered by regulators.
- Investors grow cautious as rival CoreWeave shares tumble 15% and analysts predict only 35% of announced North American data center capacity will actually get built.


Nscale, a British AI data center developer seeking to raise up to $3 billion in an initial public offering as soon as this month, faces mounting challenges as construction delays, safety violations, and technical failures plague its flagship projects across Europe and the United States. The company is targeting a valuation of as much as $35 billion at a time when investors are growing increasingly skeptical of the AI infrastructure buildout, with rival[CoreWeave](https://emergent.sh/news/coreweave-stock-price-drops-15-after-ipo) seeing its shares tumble 15% this week and Australian data center firm Firmus Grid abandoning its IPO plans after investor pushback.


## Glomfjord Flagship Site Six Months Behind Schedule


The company's Norwegian facility in Glomfjord, just north of the Arctic Circle, stands as a cautionary tale of ambitious timelines meeting operational reality. The 30-megawatt data center, designed to showcase Nscale's vertically integrated business model, has delivered only 6.4 megawatts of capacity and runs six months behind its original schedule. Construction workers are now being housed in a converted floating hotel, the Kalmar, previously used to detain migrants, as the company rushes to accelerate the buildout.


Technical setbacks have plagued the site since inception. The liquid cooling system, critical for preventing high-performance AI chips from overheating, experienced repeated leaks due to poor sealant choices and filter problems. Workers have had to switch off server rows on multiple occasions since December 2025 after discovering cooling fluid spurting onto floors. Although the faulty system was replaced in June 2026, another significant leak occurred in September due to human error.


A December 2025 transformer fire led to an investigation by Norway's Directorate for Civil Protection, which uncovered that a high-voltage cable left outside for six months had failed when connected to power. The resulting electrical arc melted metal and ignited uncovered insulation panels. Inspectors subsequently found 10 safety violations, including failure to ground exposed high-voltage components and improper registration of in-house electricians. The inspection case closed in September 2026 after Nscale resolved the issues.


## Contract Penalties and Customer Relations


Delays at Glomfjord resulted in millions of dollars in contractual penalties owed to ByteDance, the Chinese company behind TikTok that commissioned the data center. Rather than paying fines outright, customers were offered better terms in new contracts, according to people familiar with the negotiations. The pattern repeated at Nscale's Portugal site, where the company leases space at Start Campus in Sines. Delays there also triggered millions in paper penalties from Microsoft, which subsequently became leverage points for renegotiating future contract terms.


When Microsoft gained access to the Portugal facility earlier in 2026, the backup power system remained incomplete. The diagnostic platform had not been fully integrated with Microsoft's ticketing system, forcing the client to submit high-urgency tickets for every minor glitch. Operational teams struggled to distinguish between critical issues like server overheating and simple problems like missed firmware updates. The company has since implemented proper systems, but the incidents underscore execution challenges that could complicate the IPO pitch.


## Neocloud Industry Under Pressure


Nscale is one of several neoclouds, a new category of companies building massive computing facilities to serve AI developers. These firms aim to capitalize on the hundreds of billions of dollars that tech giants like Google, Microsoft, and Anthropic have pledged to spend on AI infrastructure. However, they also shoulder substantial risk, negotiating power access, managing Nvidia GPU shortages, and navigating contracts that allow customers to withdraw from commitments if delivery deadlines slip.


Market conditions have deteriorated sharply for the sector. CoreWeave's debt protection swaps now price in more than a 60% chance of default within five years. Bernstein analysts estimate only 35% of announced data center capacity in North America will actually get built, placing Nscale on their list of 10 developers with the least credible pipeline based on build stage, track record, and regulatory risk. Gartner forecasts that just 20% of neocloud providers will remain independent by 2030, highlighting the capital-intensive nature of the business.


## Vertical Integration Strategy Faces Reality


Chief Executive Officer Josh Payne has positioned vertical integration as Nscale's competitive advantage, writing in the company's S-1 filing that the strategy translates to less risk and more value for customers. The approach calls for owning the land, power, data center, chips, and software at each site. However, regulatory disclosures reveal that through August 2026, Nscale had built less than 1% of its overall targeted capacity measured in gigawatts, relying heavily on leasing from colocation providers to meet contractual obligations.


The company depends on Microsoft and Anthropic for approximately 85% of its contracts. Anthropic has committed roughly $44.6 billion for dedicated[AI chip infrastructure](https://emergent.sh/news/nvidia-h200-benchmarks-performance) at the Monarch campus in West Virginia, but Nscale's IPO filing states the company has not yet secured the financing or long-term chip supplier agreements needed to fulfill the contract. Anthropic can also withdraw from portions of the agreement without penalty if delivery tranches arrive late.


Olivier Darmouni, a financial economist at HEC Paris specializing in credit markets, describes the vertical integration ambition as too ambitious for a startup. He notes that if execution stumbles, large hyperscalers will prioritize their own data centers and exit leases, leaving Nscale investors holding the bag. The West Virginia site, while potentially scaling to 8 gigawatts, has already faced local opposition after heavy rains flooded neighboring homes with mud from denuded construction land, leading to permit violations and public backlash.


## Power Grid Constraints and Regulatory Hurdles


Access to electrical power has emerged as a critical bottleneck across Nscale's portfolio. A planned facility near London, announced in 2025 as flagship sovereign AI infrastructure for the United Kingdom, may not receive a grid connection until the early to mid-2030s. In Korgen, Norway, grid operator Statnett warned that new capacity for a planned 250-megawatt expansion is unlikely before 2037, prompting Nscale to publicly warn that investments could move to other countries.


The Glomfjord site, despite marketing itself as running on hydropower, depended on diesel generators to operate cooling systems until May 2026. Norwegian Labour Inspection Authority found the company was not keeping adequate worker records, sometimes noting only first names. After union complaints about illegal noncompete clauses in subcontractor employment agreements, Nscale severed ties with one contractor in Stavanger and renegotiated contracts in Glomfjord to eliminate subcontracting arrangements.


## Availability Timeline


Officially launched on October 15, 2026, Nscale's IPO filing comes as the company rapidly attempts to scale operations. CEO Payne announced in early October that the Texas site conversion from a bitcoin mining operation went live, nearly doubling total GPU deployments from 25,000 to more than 50,000 in less than nine months. The company has hired senior executives from established data center operators, including Microsoft's Nidhi Chappell, whose team designed the computing system used to train ChatGPT, as president of AI infrastructure.


The floating hotel Kalmar arrived in Glomfjord in early October, carrying capacity for approximately 220 workers who will attempt to accelerate construction on the delayed flagship site. Local hotels remain largely empty despite Nscale booking most available rooms since August, waiting for the construction surge. The municipality's mayor hopes to secure at least 40 permanent jobs for Glomfjord residents, though critics argue the benefits do not compensate for environmental and social disruption.


## What This Means


Nscale's struggles illustrate the execution risks inherent in the AI data center buildout, where capital commitments exceed $500 billion but delivery remains uncertain. The company's ability to close its IPO at the targeted $35 billion valuation will test investor appetite for neocloud infrastructure plays amid rising borrowing costs, construction challenges, and contract structures that favor large tech customers. With less than 1% of planned capacity operational and flagship sites experiencing repeated setbacks, Nscale must demonstrate operational maturity quickly or risk joining the predicted 80% of neocloud providers that Gartner forecasts will not remain independent through the end of the decade. The outcome will serve as a bellwether for the entire AI infrastructure sector as it transitions from speculative investment to operational reality.
